response: {"text":"Among the many ways to tackle current puzzles about electromagnetic waves—especially the challenge of fitting new experimental clues into the older wave picture—the most useful approach seems to be the careful study of the penetrating high‑energy radiation that can pass through solid matter. The advantage of this line of work does not lie mainly in the precision that can be achieved when measuring such rays, although that is valuable; it stems from the very basic character of the effects they produce. These effects reveal simple, widely applicable rules that hold across different situations, offering clear insight into how the newer quantum‑style ideas can be reconciled with classical electromagnetic theory."}
